author: Robert Carr
description: Ginger-sesame chicken and soba with edamame, browned shiitakes, sweet roasted carrots and bok choy. A measured miso-tamari sauce gets its brightness from rice vinegar and fresh lime rather than a large pour of soy sauce.
equipment: 12-inch stainless-steel skillet, such as All-Clad D5

groceryIngredients.note: Plain chicken without injected broth, salt or brine.
Trimmed caps, sliced; purchase pre-sliced for the stated prep time.
Unseasoned, ideally 0-50 mg sodium per 2 oz dry. Buckwheat-wheat soba holds up better than fragile varieties; check allergens.
17 g; compare labels, ideally no more than 650 mg sodium per tablespoon.
Choose no more than 700 mg sodium per tablespoon.
Not seasoned sushi vinegar, which adds sugar and salt.
Mild Korean red-pepper flakes, without salt.

ingredients: Chicken: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
Chicken: 2 teaspoons canola oil, allocated as 1 teaspoon for each of two batches
Roasted vegetables: 8 oz (227 g) trimmed shiitake caps, sliced 1/4 inch thick
Roasted vegetables: 12 oz (340 g) carrots, sliced into 1/4-inch-thick half-moons
Bok choy: 1 lb (454 g) baby bok choy, washed and dried; stems sliced 1/2 inch thick and leaves cut into 2-inch pieces
Bok choy: 1 teaspoon canola oil and 2 tablespoons water
Noodles: 8 oz (227 g) dry unseasoned soba and 10 cups unsalted cooking water
Edamame: 1 1/2 cups (234 g) frozen unsalted shelled edamame and 3 cups cooking water
Sauce: 1 tablespoon (17 g) white miso and 1 tablespoon (15 mL) reduced-sodium tamari
Sauce: 3 tablespoons (45 mL) unseasoned rice vinegar and 3 tablespoons (45 mL) water
Sauce: 1 tablespoon (20 g) pure maple syrup
Sauce aromatics: 2 tablespoons (24 g) finely grated fresh ginger and 3 garlic cloves (9 g peeled), finely grated
Sauce finish: 2 tablespoons (30 mL) fresh lime juice, 2 teaspoons toasted sesame oil and 1 teaspoon mild gochugaru
Toppings: 1 1/2 tablespoons (13.5 g) toasted unsalted sesame seeds and 1/4 cup (25 g) thinly sliced scallions
instructions: Start the roasted vegetables: Heat the oven to 425 F. Toss 8 oz (227 g) sliced shiitake caps and 12 oz (340 g) sliced carrots with 2 teaspoons canola oil on the sheet pan. Spread into one layer. Roast in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, turning at 12 minutes, until the mushrooms have browned edges and the carrots are tender.

Prepare and brown the chicken: Pat 1 1/2 lb (680 g) chicken pieces dry and toss with 1 tablespoon (8 g) cornstarch. Preheat the 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, then add 1 teaspoon canola oil. Add 12 oz (340 g) coated chicken in one layer. Cook undisturbed for about 3 minutes, then turn and cook 3-4 minutes more, until the thickest pieces reach 165 F. Transfer to a clean plate. Add 1 teaspoon canola oil and cook the second 12 oz (340 g) chicken batch the same way. Keep raw-chicken utensils and the cutting board away from cooked food.

Cook the edamame while the chicken browns: Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a saucepan. Add 1 1/2 cups (234 g) frozen shelled edamame and cook for the package's full cooking time, usually 4-6 minutes. Drain and set aside. Do not assume that merely thawed frozen edamame is ready to eat.

Cook the noodles: Refill the saucepan with 10 cups unsalted water and bring to a boil. Add 8 oz (227 g) dry soba. Cook for the lower end of the package's range, tasting for a tender but resilient noodle. Drain, rinse briefly under cold running water to remove loose starch and drain thoroughly again. The 8 oz quantity is the dry weight, not the cooked noodle yield.

Cook the bok choy and aromatics: After the chicken is on its clean plate, add 1 teaspoon canola oil to the skillet. Add the sliced stems from 1 lb (454 g) prepared bok choy and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the leaves from the same 1 lb bok choy and 2 tablespoons water; cover for 1-2 minutes. Uncover and let surface moisture evaporate. Stir in 2 tablespoons (24 g) grated ginger and 9 g grated garlic and cook for 30 seconds, lowering the heat if the garlic begins to color.

Make the sauce directly in the skillet: Whisk 1 tablespoon (17 g) white miso with 3 tablespoons (45 mL) water in a small cup until smooth. Add this measured miso-water mixture to the skillet along with 1 tablespoon (15 mL) reduced-sodium tamari, 3 tablespoons (45 mL) rice vinegar and 1 tablespoon (20 g) maple syrup. Stir for about 1 minute over medium heat; do not reduce it to a sticky glaze.

Combine and finish: Add the cooked chicken made from 1 1/2 lb raw chicken, the noodles cooked from 8 oz dry soba, the cooked 1 1/2 cups edamame, and the roasted vegetables made from 8 oz shiitakes and 12 oz carrots to the skillet. Use tongs to toss gently until coated and hot. Turn off the heat and add 2 tablespoons (30 mL) lime juice, 2 teaspoons toasted sesame oil and 1 teaspoon gochugaru. No extra salt or soy sauce is called for.

Portion: Weigh the finished chicken-noodle mixture and distribute it evenly among four shallow containers. Pack about 3.4 g toasted sesame seeds and 6 g sliced scallions per serving separately, using the measured totals of 13.5 g seeds and 25 g scallions. Add the toppings after reheating. Refrigerate promptly.
notes: Timing: About 55 minutes total with ready-trimmed sliced shiitakes and overlapping oven, skillet and noodle work. Two chicken batches are intentional: crowding the skillet steams the chicken. This replaces the proposed tofu recipe rather than offering tofu as the default.

Sodium: Use plain chicken without injected salt solution, unsalted edamame, unseasoned rice vinegar and lower-sodium noodles. The miso and tamari quantities are deliberately bounded. Their label values and the noodle brand can change sodium substantially; reduced-sodium does not mean sodium-free.

Meal prep: Refrigerate shallow portions at 40 F or colder within 2 hours of cooking, or 1 hour above 90 F, and use within 3-4 days. Refrigerate the scallions separately. Keep the sesame seeds dry. Rinsing and thoroughly draining the soba helps avoid carrying excess starch and water into storage.

Reheating: Add 1 tablespoon water to one chicken-noodle portion. Cover with a vented lid and microwave in short intervals, gently loosening and turning the noodles between intervals, until the chicken and noodles reach 165 F in several places. Finish with the reserved 3.4 g sesame seeds and 6 g scallions for that meal.

Freezing: Freeze portions beyond the 3-4-day refrigerated window on prep day. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat the next day. Soba and bok choy can soften after freezing; refrigerator meal prep is the preferred texture plan, not a promise of unchanged freezer quality.

Portion options: For a smaller meal, use 6 oz (170 g) dry soba instead of 8 oz for the four-serving batch, leaving chicken, edamame and vegetables unchanged. For a larger meal, use 12 oz (340 g) dry soba and add 1 extra tablespoon water per serving during reheating. Changes are not included in base nutrition.

Health-conscious review: Chicken and edamame provide protein, vegetables contribute fiber and volume, and measured canola/sesame oils replace a heavy butter or cream sauce. Buckwheat content varies: ordinary soba is not necessarily 100% buckwheat or wholly whole grain. The overall eating pattern, not a single ingredient, supports blood-pressure management.

Food-safety basis: USDA Leftovers and Food Safety, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety. Eating-pattern basis: NIH DASH, https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/dash-eating-plan.
Allergens: Soy and sesame; most soba also contains wheat. Check the miso and noodle labels. Original recipe developed for this collection; not kitchen-tested.
title: Ginger-Sesame Chicken and Soba
